[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Time-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:2-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-7) He has founded eight separate billion-dollar companies, including [XPO Logistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XPO_Logistics), [United Rentals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Rentals), and United Waste. [[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-11) ## Career [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)&action=edit§ion=2)] ### United Waste Systems (1989–1997) [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)&action=edit§ion=4)] In 1989, Jacobs founded United Waste Systems in [Greenwich, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich,_Connecticut) and began consolidating small waste collection companies that had overlapping routes in rural areas. [[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:3-15) ### United Rentals (1997) [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)&action=edit§ion=5)] In September 1997, Jacobs formed United Rentals becoming the chairman and chief executive officer of the company. During late 1997 and early 1998, the company grew through a strategy of consolidating equipment rental dealers in North America. [[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-21) He took the company public in December 1997 on the [New York Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange). [[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Antoine-18) ### XPO [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)&action=edit§ion=6)] In 2011, he invested approximately $150 million in XPO (then named _Express-1 Expedited Solutions_), a transportation and [third-party logistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-party_logistics) provider. [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-reuters-22) He became chairman of the board and CEO and gained ownership of approximately 71 percent of the company. The company was later listed on the NYSE under the ticker symbol XPO. [[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-24) ### QXO (2024–present) [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)&action=edit§ion=7)] In June 2024, Jacobs founded QXO with the intention to consolidate the $800 billion building products distribution industry. [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:2-6)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-25) With the launch, he raised over $5 billion in equity. [[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:4-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:5-29) In April 2026, QXO acquired Kodiak Building Partners,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:4-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:5-29)the fourth-largest distributor of lumber and complementary building materials in the United States, for $2.25 billion. # Brad Jacobs
## Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
QXO

Brad Jacobs has a unique track record as both a Wall Street moneymaker and business builder. He has founded and led eight companies, all of which he grew into billion-dollar or multi-billion-dollar corporations. He has completed approximately 500 M&A transactions and raised more than $50 billion in debt and equity capital, including three IPOs.

His six publicly traded companies include United Waste, United Rentals, and XPO—along with its two spin-offs, GXO Logistics and RXO—and, more recently, QXO.

Jacobs founded XPO in 2011 and led it to become one of the world’s largest freight transportation providers.

Before XPO, Jacobs founded United Rentals in 1997 and grew it to become the world’s largest equipment rental provider in just 13 months. United Rentals’ stock has since grown into a “200-bagger.”

Earlier in his career, Jacobs built United Waste into the fifth largest solid waste management company in the U.S., with its stock outperforming the S&P 500 by 5.6 times before he sold the business in 1997.

Brad Jacobs

His name is Brad Jacobs. He has built five publicly traded billion-dollar companies, in five separate industries, using more or less the same playbook each time. In 2024 he wrote the playbook down.

For the ambitious operator, his career is more instructive than the 1980s raiders precisely because he is doing it now, with the same balance-sheet structures and capital markets you have access to, in industries you can study in real time. They are the modern playbook.

500+Lifetime acquisitions completed

9 monthsUnited Rentals from founding to IPO

## United Waste, the first rollup
In 1989 he founded United Waste Systems with that exact thesis. He ran the standard rollup play.

By 1997 he had built United Waste into the country’s third-largest waste company. The trade made him personally wealthy.

## United Rentals: the IPO speed record
The same year he sold United Waste, he founded United Rentals.

## XPO Logistics: the masterclass
He installed himself as chairman and CEO. Then he ran the playbook for the third time, at the largest scale yet.

Photo by Fkbowen, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons.

The XPO acquisitions were larger than anything he had done before. By 2020 XPO was a $17 billion company.

In 2021 he started doing the reverse manoeuvre.

## Career timeline Key moments

5. 1989Founds United Waste Systems. The strategy: roll up the fragmented North American waste-hauling industry, region by region.
